title: Decide the project-local database backend for the port
description:
## Context

zic stored package and file records in datalevin (an embedded Datalog database over H2) inside the .zic-db directory. The store must support packages (name unique, version, location, metadata, dependency refs, file component refs) and files (path unique, size, class normal-file/config-file/ghost-file, SHA-256 checksum), with queries by name, dependers, dependees, file ownership (owned-by?), and (for the orphans story) non-source packages. All writes happen under an exclusive file lock (with-zic-session). Data volume is project-level (tens to hundreds of packages), and the tool's stated goal is "dead simple".

## Decision

Use a file-based store: FSet persistent maps of defstruct records, serialized as a single NRDL document in the .zic-db directory (e.g. .zic-db/packages.nrdl). Reads slurp the store into memory; writes transform the FSet map and atomically replace the file (write temp + rename) while holding the exclusive lock. Datalevin's entity refs become explicit name keys resolved with FSet lookups.

## Alternatives Considered

- (a) SQLite via cl-sqlite/cl-dbi — rejected. Verified 2026-08-12 via swanky: (asdf:load-system "cl-sqlite") fails with "Component cl-sqlite not found" in this ocicl registry. Would also add a C library dependency and a schema/query translation layer, against the "dead simple" requirement.
- (b) FSet + NRDL file store — chosen. All components verified loadable via swanky: (asdf:load-system "fset") and (asdf:load-system "com.djhaskin.nrdl") both return T. Matches dsolv's established data conventions (NRDL cards and index, FSet maps, defstruct records, emit-nrdl-struct methods), no C dependencies, atomic single-file writes, and the existing file lock already serializes writers. Unique package and file identity falls out of FSet map keys.
- (c) Lisp-native prevalence-style store (bknr.datastore, cl-prevalence) — rejected. Not present in ocicl; snapshot/journal machinery adds moving parts with no benefit at project scale.

## Consequences

- .zic-db remains the marking directory located by find-marking-file; the database file lives inside it.
- The port-db bead (zick-q6u) implements slurp-store/save-store (temp + rename), package/file defstructs, and queries as FSet lookups; serialization via nrdl:generate-to with emit-nrdl-struct methods (the dsolv pattern).
- The port-session bead (zick-lky) ensures the exclusive lock covers the read-modify-write cycle of the store file.
- The package record gains an is-source flag naturally, covering the orphans story.
acceptance_criteria: ADR recorded on this bead (Context / Decision / Alternatives Considered / Consequences). Chosen backend components verified loadable via swanky: (asdf:load-system "fset") and (asdf:load-system "com.djhaskin.nrdl") both return T. Rejected alternative cl-sqlite confirmed absent from the ocicl registry.
close_reason: Database backend decided: file-based store with FSet persistent maps serialized as NRDL in .zic-db, mirroring dsolv conventions. Components verified via swanky (fset and com.djhaskin.nrdl load; cl-sqlite not in ocicl).

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text: Verification log 2026-08-12 (swanky, port 4005): fset -> T, com.djhaskin.nrdl -> T, cl-sqlite -> Component cl-sqlite not found. Chose file-based FSet + NRDL store; this unblocks zick-q6u (port-db), zick-lky (port-session), and zick-vqv (scaffold).

title: Port the zic unit tests to Parachute
description: Port test/zic/db_test.clj, test/zic/package_test.clj (linearize: empty, basic, fighter, and cycle cases), and test/zic/session_test.clj to Parachute under tests/, wired into the com.djhaskin.zick/tests ASDF system following the style guide: each test file gets its own subpackage, parachute symbols are named in the defpackage import-from, and the asd test-op performs each package.
acceptance_criteria: (asdf:test-system "com.djhaskin.zick") passes all ported unit tests through swanky.
notes:
## Resolution

All zic unit tests are ported (linearize empty/basic/fighter/cycle, db basics, session path-to-connection-string were already in place), and the suite grew from 271 to **413 passing assertions** (120 tests across db/fs/package/session/main) with 42 new tests.

### New coverage by file
- **tests/db.lisp (+15)**: record internals (`lookup-key`, `map-contains-p`, `present-package`/`present-file` nil-dropping, `package-with-dependencies` field preservation), `:is-source` flag, `zic-paths` edge cases (nil metadata/missing keys), insert-file ownership reassignment, remove-then-reinstall, removal no-ops, unknown-package dependency queries, insert-use dedupe, empty-store and is-source/ghost round trips, corrupt-store slurp error.
- **tests/fs.lisp (+15)**: `bytes->hexstr`, per-entry SHA-256/CRC-32 known vectors, **regression test `decode-preserves-stored-crc`** (decoding an entry out-of-band must not break a later `crc-violations` check — pins the zippy CRC-clobber fix from zick-729), `directory-entry-p`, `in-set` (function/hash-table/fset-set/nil), `file-size`, empty-stream digest, `list-files`, `all-parents`, unpack overwrites existing files, backup of missing files is a no-op, verify of size-0 and directory-where-file-expected.
- **tests/package.lisp (+9)**: linearize diamond/unknown-node/self-loop, `reachable-nodes` with ignore, `sinks`, `package-file-conflicts` (clean + owner-reported), more `decide-config-fate` combinations, install signals on unmet dependency.
- **tests/session.lisp (+3)**: `with-filelock` removes the lock on signal, `with-zic-session` releases the lock on signal, `store-file-path` joins the connection directory.

### Real bug found and fixed
- **src/fs.lisp `all-parents`** walked only two levels: the loop used `for prev = nil then p` in a separate `for` clause, and CL steps separate `for` clauses sequentially, so `prev` received p's *new* value and the loop stopped after one parent. `find-marking-file` could therefore only locate `.zic-db` one directory up. Rewrote the loop as `while p collect p until (equal p (parent p))`; the new `all-parents-reaches-root` and the existing `find-marking-file-walks-up` pin the behavior.

Per the style guide, tests live in per-module subpackages under tests/, Parachute symbols are named in the defpackage `:import-from`, and the suite runs green via `(asdf:test-system "com.djhaskin.zick")` (413 ✔, exit 0), lint-clean.

title: Confirm ocicl availability of the CL libraries the port needs
description:
Map zic's JVM dependencies to Common Lisp and verify each is installable via ocicl before the module ports depend on them.

## Goal

Confirm ocicl availability for: zip handling (zippy), SHA-256 and CRC32 (ironclad), HTTP client (dexador with quri), JSON parsing for package metadata (cl-json or yason), filesystem helpers (cl-fad), file locking (sb-posix flock or equivalent), plus fset, alexandria, cl-ppcre, parachute, and the ported sibling systems com.djhaskin.cliff, com.djhaskin.nrdl, com.djhaskin.svers.

## Findings

All systems verified loadable 2026-08-12 via swanky (port 4005), each (asdf:load-system "X") returning T:

- zippy (zip archives) — OK
- ironclad (SHA-256, CRC32) — OK (first attempt hit a transient swanky EAGAIN; retry succeeded)
- dexador (HTTP client) + quri (URLs) — OK
- cl-json (JSON metadata) — OK; yason also present in ocicl if preferred
- cl-fad (filesystem helpers) — OK
- alexandria, cl-ppcre, parachute — OK
- com.djhaskin.cliff, com.djhaskin.nrdl, com.djhaskin.svers — OK (sibling ports)
- sb-posix — present in SBCL (exclusive file locking via flock for session.lisp)

Decisions recorded:

- Default output format is NRDL, not yaml (user decision 2026-08-12; zic's yaml default is dropped). CLI results print as NRDL documents via nrdl:generate-to / emit-nrdl-struct, mirroring dsolv's main.lisp. cl-yaml is loadable but not needed.
- ocicl.csv / systems.csv were not auto-generated by these loads (every system was already cached in the shared ocicl store). They will appear when a not-yet-cached system is fetched, or when the scaffold bead's com.djhaskin.zick system is first loaded; pin them then.
- If zippy does not expose per-entry CRC values, compute CRC32 by streaming each entry through ironclad's crc32 (noted for the port-fs bead).
- No quickload or qlot usage anywhere; everything resolves through ocicl/asdf.
acceptance_criteria: Final dependency list verified loadable via ocicl/asdf through swanky and recorded in Findings; no quickload/qlot usage; ocicl.csv for zick pinned when the scaffold bead first loads com.djhaskin.zick.
close_reason: All port dependencies verified loadable via swanky (zippy, ironclad, dexador, quri, cl-json, cl-fad, alexandria, cl-ppcre, parachute, fset, cliff, nrdl, svers, sb-posix). Default output format changed to NRDL per user direction.

notes:
Port of zic.cli to src/main.lisp is complete and verified.

## What was built

`src/main.lisp` now defines the `zick` command line via `cliff:execute-program`:

- Subcommands `add`, `files`, `info`, `init`, `remove`, `dependers`,
  `dependees`, `verify` (plus `list`/`orphans` stubs returning `:noop`,
  tracked by their own beads).
- zic's short aliases (`-k -V -l -m -u -w -W -d -c -C -r -R -n -N -g -G -i -I -h --help`).
- Defaults per the bead: output-format nrdl, start-directory from cwd,
  cascade false, dry-run false, download-package true.
- `setup` locates the `.zick-db` marking file at or above
  `:start-directory` (falling back to the deprecated `.zic-db` with a
  warning, per user direction) and derives db-connection-string,
  root-path, staging-path, and lock-path, mirroring zic's onecli setup.
- verify exits 3 (package not found) and 4 (verification failures) by
  extending `cliff/errors:*exit-codes*` at load time (eval-when
  :load-toplevel only, per review); missing package-name errors exit 64
  (CLIFF :cl-usage-error) with zic's exact message, deduplicated into
  the `*package-name-required*` constant.
- JSON `-m` metadata is parsed with the NRDL library (a JSON superset):
  `nrdl:parse-from` + `nrdl:to-fset` + a keywordize helper
  (keywordize-fset-map/value/seq) that interns JSON string keys as
  keywords, matching db:zick-paths' keyword-keyed metadata maps. This
  removed the cl-json dependency entirely (dropped from the .asd).
- Results print as NRDL documents (CLIFF default), so no custom
  output handling was needed beyond the result maps.

## Tests

`tests/main.lisp` grew from 3 smoke tests to 18 integration tests (all
CLI commands run against real temporary projects, with a throwaway
HTTP server for the download path): init creates the store, add -W
records + info shows, -u drives dependers/dependees, missing -k exits
64 for all six query/remove subcommands, missing add args signal,
unmet dependency signals, download + unpack + files + verify 0, tamper
gives verify 4, unknown package gives verify 3, JSON metadata marks
config files (deleting one fails verify 4), remove then info reports
not-found, remove-without-cascade refuses, and the deprecated `.zic-db`
fallback warns while still working. The suite's `-d` values are passed
without a trailing slash so the real-world path shape is always
exercised.

## Findings / bugs caught

1. **Real bug caught by binary e2e (not by in-process tests):** a
   `-d` path without a trailing slash parses as a *file* pathname, so
   init's `(merge-pathnames ".zick-db/" start)` created the store in
   the *parent* directory and setup's find-marking-file never checked
   the start directory's own contents. Fixed by
   `uiop:ensure-directory-pathname` in both `init!` and `setup`.
   In-process tests had passed because `native-namestring` of a
   directory pathname keeps the trailing slash; the binary exposed it.
2. **gmap limitations in the pinned ocicl snapshot:** `:result
   fset:seq` and `:arg :map`-to-`:result fset:map` are not registered
   (only `:result list/alist/...`); fset seqs are not plain lists
   (`listp` is NIL), so `(:arg :list seq)` fails — use `:arg :seq`
   with `:result list` + `f:convert 'fset:seq`.
3. **fmt.ros instability** bit hard on the new file (etypecase clause
   merging; docstring + let* collapse into 100-140-char lines; the
   init! body). Hand-fixed; fmt must not be re-run on main.lisp (its
   canonical output violates its own 80-char lint). New findings
   appended to bead zick-vo7.
4. **ASDF fasl staleness** during development: after the file was
   truncated mid-edit, a balanced-but-truncated main.lisp compiled
   successfully and left a stale fasl that masked the missing
   functions; rm the fasl + force recompile to recover.

## Validation

- Full suite: 488 checkmarks, 363 passed / 0 failed (was 3 smoke
  tests at the start of this bead).
- lint (line lengths) clean; lisp-check-parens clean on all files.
- Binary builds via ./scripts/build; real executable e2e verified:
  help 0, init creates .zick-db/packages.nrdl in the project, add -W,
  info, verify 3/0, dependers/dependees, remove cascade-refusal,
  missing -k → 64.
- Acceptance criteria met: help/init/add/info/files/verify/remove/
  dependers/dependees run against a test database; verify exits 3/4 in
  the right cases; missing package-name errors are raised.

title: Fix infinite loop: relative -d start directory hangs all-parents
description:
## Summary

`zick` spins forever (99% CPU) when started with a **relative** start
directory: `zick init -d .` (or any relative `-d PATH`).  Absolute
`-d /abs/path` works, and omitting `-d` (cwd default) works.

## Reproduction

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/p && cd /tmp/p && zick init -d .
# hangs forever, 99% CPU; kill -9 required
```

With `-d /tmp/p` or no `-d` at all, `init` completes instantly.

## Root cause

`src/fs.lisp` `all-parents`: it walks `pathname-parent-directory-pathname`
from the start path, stopping once a directory equals its own parent (the
filesystem root).  With a relative pathname, the parent chain grows
indefinitely (`".."` → `"../.."` → `"../../.."` …) and never equals its own
parent, so the loop never terminates.  `find-marking-file` calls
`all-parents` on the start directory, so any relative `-d` hangs.

Absolute pathnames reach a parent that equals itself, so they terminate.

## Fix ideas

- Normalize the start directory to an absolute pathname early in the
  chain: `setup` in `src/main.lisp` already parses `:start-directory`
  with `uiop:parse-native-namestring` — `uiop:truename` /
  `uiop:merge-pathnames*` against `(uiop:getcwd)` would make it
  absolute, and `init-command` could do the same.
- Or harden `all-parents` to stop after a bounded number of steps /
  detect the `..` growth pattern directly.

## Notes

- Found while verifying tutorial docs (bead zick-e4d.2): the quickstart
  used `zick init -d .` copy-paste style.  Docs should prefer omitting
  `-d` (cwd default) or use absolute paths until fixed.
- The swank-server probe confirmed the store/session logic itself is
  fine; the hang is purely the marking-file search.

title: Convention: take the lock first, and rename zic to zick throughout the port
description: Session convention decided 2026-08-12 with the maintainer: (1) In every place a session/lock is used, take the exclusive file lock BEFORE opening the database (slurp), never after; this avoids lost updates between concurrent zick sessions on a plain file store. with-zic-session must therefore be lock-first, and any future caller of with-database/with-filelock must follow the same order. (2) Any instance of the string/name "zic" in the port should be changed to "zick": the lock error message says "Probably another zick process is running.", the store directory is .zick-db, and the lock file is .zick.lock (matching the existing zick-4me ADR naming). zic/session.clj reference code keeps its own names.
acceptance_criteria: No remaining bare "zic" references in zick source or docs; lock acquisition precedes db open in session.lisp and in the CLI port (zick-qlg).
notes:
## Summary

Bead zick-95h ("Convention: take the lock first; rename zic → zick throughout the port") is complete.

## Lock-first convention — already satisfied, verified

`with-zick-session` (src/session.lisp) takes the lock **before** opening the
database: `with-filelock lock-path` wraps `with-database connection-string`,
so two concurrent zick sessions serialize on the lock before either reads the
store. Its docstring documents this ordering. The bead's locking requirement
needed no code change.

## zic → zick rename — applied throughout the port

Per your decision ("Rename all of them" for port names, "Keep them as zic" for
provenance references), all port-owned names were renamed:

- `with-zic-session` → `with-zick-session` (src/session.lisp, src/package.lisp,
  tests/session.lisp, CHANGELOG.md)
- `zic-paths` → `zick-paths` (src/db.lisp, src/package.lisp, tests/db.lisp)
- `:zic` NRDL metadata key → `:zick` (src/db.lisp + fixture data in tests)
- `.zic-db` marking file → `.zick-db` (src/fs.lisp, src/db.lisp, tests/fs.lisp,
  CHANGELOG.md)
- `zick.lock` → `.zick.lock` test lock-file convention (tests/session.lisp,
  tests/package.lisp)

Remaining bare `zic` references are all provenance (comments citing zic's
source files/tests, "ported from zic", CHANGELOG history) — kept per your call.

## Verification

- Full suite: **310 ✔, 0 failed** in a **fresh** `ros run` process. (The
  long-lived swanky image holds stale pre-rename symbols and must not be used
  for verification after renames; a fresh process compiles from source and
  passes.)
- fmt --check clean (idempotent), paren-check balanced on all 8 touched files.
- Code review passed with two checks confirmed clean:
  1. src/session.lisp never hardcodes a lock filename (`with-filelock` takes
     the path; tests pass `.zick.lock` explicitly) — no source/test mismatch.
  2. The `:zic`→`:zick` sed only touched the NRDL metadata key and fixture
     metadata maps — no `:zic` used as a data value/package name anywhere.

## Notes / follow-ups

- **Backward compat (intentional, pre-1.0):** renaming the `:zic` metadata key
  and the `.zick-db` marking file changes the on-disk store format and the
  working-tree marker. Stores and trees created by earlier zick versions are
  not recognized by this build. This is an accepted breaking change during the

notes:
## Summary

Bead zick-rbg (update a package that already exists via install) —
the upgrade machinery (`upgrade-existing-package`, serovers
in-place/downgrade guards, backup/.new naming, put-aside/do-nothing
config fates, stale-file removal) was already implemented and tested;
the acceptance criterion's "updates the database record" clause and a
real end-to-end upgrade path were the genuine gaps.  Closing them
exposed and fixed a real bug in `-m` JSON metadata keywordization.

## Bug found and fixed (src/main.lisp)

`zick add -m` silently ignored its metadata: NRDL reads JSON object
keys back as **case-preserved keywords** (e.g. `:|zick|`, not
`:zick` and not strings), so `keywordize-fset-map`'s old
`(if (stringp k) (intern k :keyword) k)` never fired (symbols passed
through untouched), and even genuine string keys were interned
lowercase (`(intern "zick" :keyword)` is `:|zick|`, not `:zick` —
`intern` does not upcase).  Consequence: `db:zick-paths` lookups for
`:zick`/`:config-files` returned nil, so config-file classification,
ghost files, and therefore upgrade put-aside/do-nothing decisions
were silently disabled for every CLI-installed package.

Fix: `keywordize-fset-map` now normalizes both string and symbol keys
via `(intern (string-upcase ...) :keyword)`.  Idempotent for already
uppercase keywords; nested maps/seqs still recurse; string *values*
(like config-file paths) are untouched.  The auth path
(`keywordize-auth-record`) already upcased and was unaffected (it
reads `nrdl:parse-from`'s string keys directly; `test-download-auth`
still passes).

The old `add-with-json-metadata-marks-config-files` test masked this:
it only checked that verify fails after deleting the file, which also
happens when a normal file goes missing.  It now asserts the `files`
output shows `class config-file` and `class normal-file`, and a new
`json-metadata-keywordizes-nrdl-keys` test pins the
`json-metadata-to-fset` → `zick-paths` contract directly.

## Acceptance criterion coverage

"Upgrading b 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 over an existing install preserves
edited config files (put-aside), removes stale normal files, and
updates the database record."

- **preserves edited config files (put-aside)**: already covered by
  `config-precautions-upgrade` / `install-package-upgrade-backs-up-on-disk`
  (edited conf kept in place, incoming one put aside as
  `conf.txt.<pkg>.<ver>.new`); the new black-box `test-add-upgrade`
  proves it through the real CLI (user-edited `u/conf.txt` survives,
  `conf.txt.u.0.2.0.new` holds the incoming version).
- **removes stale normal files**: `install-package-upgrade-backs-up-on-disk`
  (old normal file deleted) and `test-add-upgrade` (`u/stale.txt` gone
  from disk and from the record after the 0.2.0 upgrade).
- **updates the database record**: NEW — `install-package-upgrade-backs-up-on-disk`
  now slurps the persisted store after a real download upgrade and
  asserts version 0.2.0, the new file set (conf.txt/app.txt present,
  oldconf.txt gone), and conf.txt retaining `:config-file` class;
  `test-add-upgrade` asserts `info` shows `version "0.2.0"` and `files`
  shows the config-file/normal-file classes with no stale entry.

Also exercised (pre-existing, still green): backup naming
(`oldconf.txt.a.0.1.0.backup`), `.new` naming, in-place refusal
(`allow-inplace`), downgrade refusal (`allow-downgrades`).

## New/changed artifacts

- `src/main.lisp`: keywordize-fset-map bugfix (string AND symbol keys
  → uppercase keywords).
- `tests/package.lisp`: `install-package-upgrade-backs-up-on-disk`
  strengthened with the DB-record assertions.
- `tests/main.lisp`: `add-with-json-metadata-marks-config-files`
  asserts file classes in `files` output; new
  `json-metadata-keywordizes-nrdl-keys` contract test.
- `tests/resources/fixture/make-fixtures.sh`: `u.zip`/`u2.zip` pair —
  both carry the same `u/` entry prefix (the install path follows the
  zip's own prefix); v1 = conf.txt (config) + app.txt + stale.txt,
  v2 = changed conf/app + new.txt, stale dropped.
- `tests/resources/scripts/test-add-upgrade`: full CLI upgrade
  black-box test.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Fixed entry for the `-m` metadata keywordization bug.

## Quality gates

  strengthened assertions run as new checks).
- Black-box: all 11 scripts pass, including the new test-add-upgrade.
- `fmt.ros --check` clean; `lisp-check-parens` level 0; no lines over

- Code review applied: direct contract test for the keywordization,
  CHANGELOG entry for the user-visible bugfix.

title: Design and implement the list command
description: zic.cli/list! is a FIXME no-op. Decide the scope of zick list (installed packages with name and version, possibly file counts), implement it in CLIFF emitting NRDL output (the default output-format), document it, and cover it with black-box tests. This goes beyond the original code, so record the design decision on the bead.

notes:
## zick-uot — Design and implement the list command

### Design decision (recorded on the bead)

zic's `list!` was a FIXME no-op, so the bead's "Decide the scope of
zick list" is literal.  Scope chosen: **every installed package with
its name and version, sorted by name**.  The bead's "possibly file
counts" was decided against for now: it would make the query
O(packages × files) (each count needs a scan of the files map) for a
column the acceptance criterion doesn't require, and the NRDL shape is
additive — a `file-count` key can be added later without breaking
consumers.  The explicit `sort` on the presented infos is deliberate:
it pins the output contract in code rather than relying on FSet's map
iteration order.

Empty-database behavior follows the acceptance criterion exactly
("prints nothing and exits 0"): the command returns the
`:cliff-suppress-output` key, which CLIFF honors by skipping NRDL
generation entirely (verified in cliff/src/main.lisp, and pinned by the

title: Cover the download-package! path and on-disk precaution effects in tests/package.lisp
description:
Code review of the zic.package port (bead zick-e22) flagged coverage gaps:

1. download-package! (URL fetch via dexador, staging-directory creation, URL-filename fallback) has zero test coverage — every install test uses :download-package nil. Add one integration test installing from a local URL (file:// or throwaway HTTP server) asserting the recorded package plus staged-zip handling.

2. The config precaution tests assert in-memory decisions but not on-disk effects: fresh-install checks the :put-aside set but never verifies conf.txt was actually backed up/moved on disk; the upgrade test doesn't assert the put-aside file landed in the backup location. Assert backup-file existence to pin fs:backup-all behavior (where the fset-set bug lived).

3. remove-package's config-file backup-on-removal branch is untested (all remove tests use packages without config files).
notes:
## Resolution

All three coverage gaps are closed in tests/package.lisp (271 tests green).

### New tests
- `download-package-fetches-to-staging`: downloads a zip from a throwaway local HTTP server, asserts the archive contents and that the zip is staged under the URL's last path component.
- `download-package-fallback-filename`: URL with no path component falls back to NAME-VERSION.zip.
- `download-package-requires-name-version-location`: signals without name/version/location.
- `install-package-downloads-from-url`: end-to-end install from a URL (recorded package + files, unpacked files on disk, put-aside of an existing conf.txt, staged zip kept).
- `install-package-upgrade-backs-up-on-disk`: upgrade via download backs up old config files absent from the new version (name.version.backup), deletes old normal files, puts aside edited configs.
- `remove-package-backs-up-config-files`: removal backs up config files on disk and deletes normal files.

### Real bugs found and fixed along the way
1. **src/package.lisp** `download-package`: `:staging-path` was string-only (`uiop:parse-native-namestring`); it now accepts pathnames or strings, matching how `:root-path` is handled everywhere else.
2. **src/fs.lisp** zip CRC clobbering: zippy's `decode-entry` overwrites an entry's stored CRC with its local file header value (0 for data-descriptor zips). `upgrade-existing-package` computed archive checksums before `fs:unpack`'s `crc-violations` check, causing false "CRC violations" errors on valid zips. Fixed with `with-entry-crc-preserved` in `entry-sha256`/`entry-crc`.
3. **Test fixtures**: `write-source-fixture` created a spurious empty `x/` directory that leaked into zips; three download tests mixed `root` and `proj` (root-path vs. where assertions read files); the fallback test's bare URL matched the regex via its port number. All corrected.

### Test infrastructure
- The throwaway HTTP server (`http-serve-once`) uses usocket + bordeaux-threads + flexi-streams (latin-1 wrapper over a binary socket so arbitrary zip bytes round-trip), added to the test system's deps in com.djhaskin.zick.asd. Serving one connection, closing the stream (not the usocket object) so dexador sees EOF, and `\r\n` response line endings were the keys to making dexador happy.

title: Make fmt.ros stable: cl-indentify formatting is not idempotent and fights its own lint
description:
## Summary

`fmt.ros` (`.agents/skills/djha-skin-common-lisp/scripts/fmt.ros`) is **unstable**: running it repeatedly on the same file keeps changing the file (no fixed point), its canonical output violates its own `--check` line-length lint, and hand-fixing lint findings is undone by the next format run. Encountered at length while porting `zic.package` (bead `zick-e22`); everything found is documented below for revisitation.

## Findings (empirically observed unless noted)

### 1. Not idempotent — no fixed point
Running `ros fmt.ros <file>` twice is not a no-op the second time. cl-indentify's `indentify` *joins* short forms onto single lines ("merges") and, once a merge exists in the file, subsequent runs **preserve** the merged state instead of splitting it back. Merges accumulate and cascade; each run can produce different output. Observed merges:

- A `(let*` got joined onto the closing line of an `error` string form in `verify-package-files` (src/package.lisp, ~lines 94-102).
- Short `lambda` bodies were joined into single long lines.
- A `defun` docstring got pushed far right past 80 chars by the formatter's alignment (src/session.lisp line 30, 97 chars).

### 2. Formatter output fails its own lint
cl-indentify's canonical indentation places deeply nested forms at large columns (e.g. `gmap` with `(:arg :seq ...)` nested several levels deep), producing lines over the 80-char `*max-line-length*`, which `--check` then flags. So `fmt` produces code that fails `fmt --check` — the two modes of the same tool contradict each other.

### 3. Fix-by-hand is undone by the next run
Because of the merge cascade, hand-shortening over-long lines and re-running `fmt` re-merges them again. The file never converges to a state where `fmt --check` passes. The only workable strategy found: restructure code for shallower nesting (extract helpers such as `config-group-paths`, `install-with-download`), run `fmt` **once**, then hand-fix remaining long lines and **do not re-run fmt** before committing.

### 4. Merging is context-dependent, not reproducible in isolation
Fresh-file probes containing the identical form bodies (`/tmp/fmt-probe.lisp`, `/tmp/fmt-probe2.lisp`) did **not** merge when formatted, but the same bodies inside the real file did. Root cause unknown — suggests cl-indentify behavior depends on surrounding context and/or on pre-existing (already-merged) line structure in the file.

### 5. Pre-existing lint debt blocks `--check` as a gate
`src/db.lisp` lines 275 and 358 already exceed 80 chars, so `fmt.ros --check` fails on the existing tree regardless of new code. Until the debt is cleared (or the check is scoped to changed lines), `--check` cannot be used as a quality gate.

### 6. Lint vs. house-style docstring conflict
Formatter alignment pushes `defun` docstrings past 80 chars; house style prefers `;;;` comments above top-level definitions anyway. This motivated converting the `with-filelock` docstring in src/session.lisp to a `;;;` comment.

## Code-level observations (from reading fmt.ros; suspected, not all confirmed)

- `register-macro-templates` and `system` are **dead code**: `main` never calls them, so auto-detected macro `&body` templates are never registered and macros like `gmap` fall back to default templates. Either wire them up or delete them.
- `lint-file`'s defpackage tracking ends when it sees a line matching `^\s*\)\s*$` — a lone `)` line inside a defpackage form prematurely ends tracking; tracking is line-based, not form-based, and fragile for multi-line defpackages.
- `*keyword-export-re*` (`\s:(\S+)\s`) requires whitespace *after* the keyword, so `:foo)` at end of line is missed; it also scans whole lines with no string/comment awareness (potential false positives inside strings/comments).
- `*max-line-length*` applies uniformly to all files with no way to exempt/ignore specific lines.

## Suggested direction

Replace or augment the cl-indentify formatting with an idempotent approach: a run-until-stable loop with a fixed-point check (compare output to input; fail if it changed), a lint guaranteed consistent with the formatter (or drop the formatter in favor of a pure linter plus targeted fixes), and clear the db.lisp debt so `--check` can gate. Consider asserting `fmt(fmt(x)) == fmt(x)` in the test suite.
acceptance_criteria: fmt(fmt(x)) == fmt(x) for all project sources; fmt --check passes clean on the whole tree
notes:
## Resolution (2026-08-12)

Fixed in `.agents/skills/djha-skin-common-lisp/scripts/fmt.ros`. All three
findings are addressed:

1. **Idempotence**: `format-file` now seeks a fixed point explicitly — it
   re-runs `indentify` until output stops changing (max 10 passes) and only
   writes the file when the *final* stable output differs from the input.
   Oscillation (A→B→A) is detected and signals an error instead of writing.
   The earlier "never converges" symptom was a control-flow bug: `(return
   pass)` only exited the loop and execution fell through to the error
   signal, so every successful format reported failure. Replaced with
   `return-from` plus cycle detection.

2. **Lint vs. format contradiction**: the 80-char violations were caused by
   cl-indentify's *alignment* style — continuation arguments align under the
   first argument (the "match parens" rule in `scan-forms`), so deeply
   nested forms (gmap lambdas, define-test bodies, multiple-value-bind
   continuations, f:with values) landed far past column 80. Fix: register
   compact **body templates** that indent two spaces instead of aligning:
   - `DEFINE-TEST` → `(:count 1 :sub (nil (:count 0) nil))`
   - `GMAP:GMAP` → `(:count 1 :sub (nil (:count 0) nil))`
   - `F:WITH` / `FSET:WITH` → `(:count 2 :sub (nil nil (:count 0) nil))`
   - plus the existing `WITH-ZIP-FILE` / `WITH-DATABASE` / `WITH-ZIC-SESSION`
     / `WITH-FILELOCK` entries and the file-local `defmacro` scanner.
   Templates are keyed by name *string*, which is the only form that applies
   to internal (non-exported) macros — the symbol method only registers
   external symbols. Result: `fmt --check` passes clean on the whole tree
   (was 24 lines over 80 across 5 files).

3. **Hand-fixes no longer undone**: with a stable fixed point, editing a
   file and re-running fmt is safe. Verified: a second `fmt` run is a no-op
   (identical git diff).

Dead code removed: the unused `register-macro-templates` call (a no-op) and
the `system` parameter. `register-file-macro-templates` (the defmacro
scanner, previously dead) is now actually wired into `main` and registers
file-local macros like `with-temporary-directory`.

Quality gates: full suite 241 ✔ / 0 ✘; `fmt --check` clean on whole tree;
parens balanced everywhere.

Remaining known gaps (separate bead): the `--check` reformat-detection
feature was dropped from the final rewrite (the fixed-point check covers it
via `formatted-p`), and `*keyword-export-re*` still misses a couple of
defpackage edge cases. Note the formatter still only *re-indents* — it never
wraps long lines; keeping lines under 80 requires the compact templates
above, not line wrapping.
## Finding 2026-08-12: etypecase clauses with nested gmap/convert bodies are merged onto one line

While porting zic.cli (bead zick-qlg), fmt.ros merged the f:seq clause of an etypecase onto the previous clause line:

    (f:map (keywordize-fset-map value))    (f:seq (f:convert 'fset:seq' ...

producing a 110-char line, violating its own 80-char --check, and creating a non-fixed-point (the next fmt run reformats again). Hand-fixing the output made --check report "Not at formatting fixed point"; the only stable solution was restructuring the code so each etypecase clause body is a short single call (extract a keywordize-fset-seq helper).
